doors.when: Before starting or joining a team repository, to learn whether the clone already holds a Crew workspace and which desk a session there binds

errors.means: The folder given with --repo, or the current folder, is not inside a Git clone.
errors.fix: Pass --repo with the path of the team's clone.

errors.means: The clone is a Git repository but holds no Crew workspace yet.
errors.fix: Run crew start in it to set one up, or point --repo at the team's real clone.

doors.when: Turning a new or existing repository into a team workspace with roster, desks template and config, previewed first and landed with --apply
doors.confirm: With --apply this commits, pushes and opens and merges a pull request on the team's GitHub repository; go ahead?

errors.means: A check before any write stopped it, such as a file Crew would add already existing or a bad founder alias.
errors.fix: Act on the sentence in the result's message, then run start again.

errors.means: The repository is already a Crew workspace, so there is nothing to start.
errors.fix: Have each teammate run crew join in their own clone instead.

errors.means: The shared write stopped at the stage the result names, such as push or pull_request, and the clone was put back.
errors.fix: Fix what the reason names, for example the gh sign-in, then run the same command again.

errors.means: The pull request opened but has not merged yet.
errors.fix: Run the same command again to retry the merge, or merge that pull request by hand.

doors.when: Adding a member's roster row and own desk folder to an existing team workspace, or adopting a reviewed existing desk
doors.confirm: With --apply this pushes a desk folder and opens and merges a roster pull request on the team's GitHub repository; go ahead?

errors.means: The clone has no Crew workspace to join.
errors.fix: Ask the team for the right repository, or run crew start to found one.

errors.means: The identity already has a roster row, so nothing was added.
errors.fix: Start a Desk session in this clone signed in to gh as that identity.

errors.means: A check stopped the join before any write, such as a missing identity, a bad alias or a desk folder that may be someone else's.
errors.fix: Act on the result's message, or preview again and pass --adopt-existing with the reviewed commit.

errors.means: The join stopped at a named stage such as history, alias, desk or verify.
errors.fix: Fix what the reason in parentheses names, then run the same join again.

errors.means: The desk is pushed but the roster row waits in an unmerged pull request.
errors.fix: Run the same join again to retry the merge, which reuses that pull request.

doors.when: Opening a fresh team initiative folder with a card template in the working tree, ready to fill in and publish by pull request

errors.means: The clone is not a Crew workspace, so it has no _shared/tracks to write into.
errors.fix: Point --repo at the team's Crew clone.

errors.means: The slug given has no letters or digits to build a folder name from.
errors.fix: Pass a short name such as reliability-checks.

errors.means: A folder or file with that slug is already under _shared/tracks, and nothing changed.
errors.fix: Contribute to the existing card, or pick another slug.

doors.when: Moving a loose plan file or folder into the team's tracks as a proper initiative with a README card

errors.means: The file or folder named does not exist.
errors.fix: Check the path and rerun with the right one.

errors.means: The source is the whole tracks folder or the repository itself.
errors.fix: Name the one file or folder that holds the initiative.

errors.means: The target folder or file under _shared/tracks already exists.
errors.fix: Pass --slug with another name.

errors.means: The source is a symbolic link.
errors.fix: Pass the file the link points to instead.

doors.when: Auditing the team's _shared/tracks layout for loose files or folders lacking a README card, with the adopt command that fixes each

errors.means: Some entries under _shared/tracks are loose files or folders with no README.md card.
errors.fix: Run the crew initiative adopt command printed next to each entry.

errors.means: The folder checked is not inside a Git clone.
errors.fix: Pass --repo with the team clone's path.

doors.when: Finding this agent's own Copilot session id from its process tree, for example to give as a reply address

errors.means: On Windows the command cannot walk process parents, since it relies on ps.
errors.fix: Read the id from the session folder name or the app, and pass it with send --from.

doors.when: Reading the latest user and assistant turns of another local session, by id, prefix or name, before messaging it

errors.means: The count argument is not a positive whole number.
errors.fix: Give a count such as 6, or leave it out.

errors.means: No single session here matches the reference, or it has no events.jsonl on this machine.
errors.fix: Pass the full session id, or run the command on the machine hosting that session.

doors.when: Messaging another agent session through the Copilot app, with a sender header, then waiting until the text shows in its history

errors.means: The reference names no session here, or matches several.
errors.fix: Pass the full session id; tail shows which session is which.

errors.means: The Copilot app's local socket files are missing or their owner process has exited.
errors.fix: Open the app, then run the same send again.

errors.means: The app answered but did not accept the message, perhaps because the session is archived.
errors.fix: Pass the id of a session open in the app.

doors.when: Executing one pending Desk migration that the startup line named, with Detect, Safety check, Migrate and its announcement

errors.means: Desk's migrations folder has no migration with that id.
errors.fix: Pass the exact id the startup migrations line printed, such as 02-tidy-desk.

errors.means: No bash was found to run the migration's blocks.
errors.fix: Install bash, then run the same migration again.

doors.when: Producing the archive of production node modules the desk server loads, for one platform, CPU and Node ABI

errors.means: A production dependency has no entry in package-lock.json.
errors.fix: Run npm install in plugins/desk/mcp so the lock lists it, then build again.

errors.means: A dependency's installed folder holds no runtime file to pack.
errors.fix: Reinstall node_modules so the package's own files are present.

errors.means: A dependency file's path is too long for a tar header.
errors.fix: Shorten or flatten that dependency's install path, then build again.

doors.when: Confirming a built dependency archive still matches the package lock and the target platform, CPU and Node ABI

errors.means: The pack is missing a file, targets an unsupported platform, or its manifest, checksum or archive disagree with the lock.
errors.fix: Rebuild it with npm run runtime:deps-pack:build.

errors.means: The lock has no entry for a production dependency, so the expected pack cannot be derived.
errors.fix: Run npm install in plugins/desk/mcp, rebuild the pack and verify again.

doors.when: A runner's periodic cycle reading GitHub for each watched repository and collecting the wakes it should deliver now

errors.means: The drains config is not valid JSON or an entry is malformed, so nothing was polled
errors.fix: Correct the entry named in the message against docs/issue-drains.md and poll again

errors.means: The drains config exists but cannot be read, usually a permissions or owner change
errors.fix: Restore read permission on the config file and poll again

errors.means: Another live poll or ack holds the drains lock file
errors.fix: Wait for that process to finish, then poll again

doors.when: After a runner delivers (or fails to deliver) an issue wake, to clear or keep that repository's waiting events

errors.means: A poll or another ack holds the drains lock, so the delivery was not recorded
errors.fix: Run the wake's done command again once that process exits

errors.means: With --error, the drains config is read to start a successor session and it is malformed
errors.fix: Fix the bad entry in the drains config, then rerun the done command with --error

doors.when: Checking drain health: last good poll, lag, waiting events, quota, relay lines and stuck desk saves

errors.means: The drains config has a bad entry, so no status lines could be built
errors.fix: Repair the entry the message names, then ask for status again

errors.means: The drains config file is present but its permissions block reading it
errors.fix: Give your user read access to the file and rerun status

doors.when: Explaining why a particular issue woke its session, or what one named relay fired, merged or waits on

errors.means: The target is not written as owner/name#number
errors.fix: Pass an issue such as owner/name#123, or --relay with a relay name

errors.means: relays.json is malformed, and why reads it before answering about issues or relays
errors.fix: Correct relays.json against docs/relays.md and ask again

errors.means: relays.json exists but cannot be read by this user
errors.fix: Fix the file's permissions, then rerun why

doors.when: A runner cycle collecting the timed prompts now due, running each schedule's when gate first

errors.means: schedules.json is not valid JSON or one schedule entry is malformed
errors.fix: Correct the schedule the message names against docs/schedules.md and poll again

errors.means: schedules.json is present but cannot be read, often after an owner or permission change
errors.fix: Restore read access to schedules.json and poll again

errors.means: Another schedule poll or ack holds schedule.lock
errors.fix: Wait for that process to end, then rerun the schedule poll

doors.when: After a runner hands over a scheduled prompt, to move the schedule's next run on or keep it due

errors.means: schedule.lock is held by a live schedule poll or ack, so nothing was recorded
errors.fix: Rerun the wake's done command after the other process finishes

doors.when: Seeing each timed prompt's next run, last delivery and gate result without moving anything

errors.means: A schedule entry in schedules.json is malformed, so no lines were listed
errors.fix: Repair that schedule entry, then list the schedules again

errors.means: schedules.json cannot be read because of its owner or permissions
errors.fix: Make schedules.json readable by your user and rerun schedule status

doors.when: A runner cycle finding idle sessions whose focused card is unfinished and offering each a single nudge

errors.means: stalled.json is not valid JSON or has a bad idleMinutes, maxIdleHours or desks value
errors.fix: Correct stalled.json against docs/stalled-nudges.md and poll again

errors.means: stalled.json exists but cannot be read, usually a permissions change
errors.fix: Restore read access to stalled.json and poll again

errors.means: Another stalled poll or ack holds stalled.lock
errors.fix: Let that process finish, then rerun the stalled poll

doors.when: After a runner delivers an idle-session nudge, to end that stretch's nudge or keep it offered on failure

errors.means: stalled.lock belongs to a live stalled poll or ack, so the outcome was not saved
errors.fix: Run the nudge's done command again once the lock holder exits

doors.when: A dry run showing which idle sessions would get a nudge and why other focused sessions are left alone

errors.means: stalled.json has a malformed setting, so no sessions were checked
errors.fix: Fix the setting the message names, then rerun stalled status

errors.means: stalled.json cannot be read by this user
errors.fix: Make stalled.json readable and rerun stalled status

doors.when: Counting what a card has shipped: merged pull requests GitHub confirms and named acceptance passes from outcomes rather than messages, commits or busy

errors.means: No card was given, so nothing was counted
errors.fix: Pass --card with a card id from the turn-end ledger

doors.when: A runner cycle letting each due relay dispatch workflows, comment on and merge green labelled pull requests
doors.confirm: This can dispatch workflows, post status comments and merge pull requests on GitHub; run the relays now?

errors.means: relays.json is not valid JSON or a relay entry is malformed, so no relay ran
errors.fix: Correct the relay the message names against docs/relays.md and poll again

errors.means: relays.json exists but its permissions block reading it
errors.fix: Restore read access to relays.json and poll again

errors.means: Another relays poll holds the relays lock file
errors.fix: Wait for that poll to end, then run relays poll again

doors.when: Reading each relay's last poll, last fire or merge, spend, and what it waits on, without acting on GitHub

errors.means: relays.json has a malformed relay, so no lines were listed
errors.fix: Repair that relay entry, then list the relays again

errors.means: relays.json cannot be read because of its owner or permissions
errors.fix: Make relays.json readable by your user and rerun relays status

doors.when: A runner cycle downloading webhook events from the receiver to local payload files and printing their wakes

errors.means: hooks.json is not valid JSON, has a bad entry, or lists hooks without a server
errors.fix: Correct hooks.json against docs/webhooks.md and poll again

errors.means: hooks.json exists but cannot be read, usually a permissions change
errors.fix: Restore read access to hooks.json and poll again

errors.means: Another hooks poll or ack holds hooks.lock
errors.fix: Wait for that process to finish, then rerun hooks poll

doors.when: After a webhook wake lands, to delete exactly its listed events on the receiver, or keep them all on failure
doors.confirm: This deletes the listed webhook events from the hooks receiver; acknowledge them?

errors.means: hooks.json no longer has a hook by that name, likely removed after the wake was printed
errors.fix: Leave the events; the receiver expires them after 7 days

errors.means: hooks.json is malformed, so the hook to acknowledge could not be found
errors.fix: Repair hooks.json, then rerun the wake's done command

errors.means: hooks.lock is held by a live hooks poll or ack
errors.fix: Rerun the done command once that process exits

doors.when: Registering a new webhook endpoint on the receiver for a sender such as Stripe, Sentry or GitHub
doors.confirm: This creates a hook on the hooks receiver and prints its signing secret once; create it?

errors.means: The name is not 1 to 40 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens
errors.fix: Pick a name such as spoonjoy-sentry and run create again

errors.means: The chosen --verify preset checks the sender's signing secret, and none came on stdin
errors.fix: Pipe the sender's secret in and add --secret-stdin

errors.means: The chosen --verify preset takes no secret, yet --secret-stdin was given
errors.fix: Run create again without --secret-stdin

errors.means: No receiver is named: neither --server nor a server in hooks.json
errors.fix: Pass --server https://<receiver> or set "server" in hooks.json

errors.means: The receiver answered with an HTTP error, for example 401 for the account's token
errors.fix: Check gh auth token for that account, or retry if the receiver was briefly down

errors.means: The GitHub CLI produced no token for the account that signs in
errors.fix: Run gh auth login --hostname github.com for that account

doors.when: Inspecting every webhook the receiver holds for your account, including unrouted ones and recent rejections

errors.means: Neither --server nor hooks.json names a receiver to ask
errors.fix: Add --server https://<receiver>, or put "server" in hooks.json

errors.means: The receiver refused the listing with an HTTP error status
errors.fix: Confirm the account's gh token works, then list again

errors.means: gh auth token returned nothing for the chosen account
errors.fix: Sign the account into the GitHub CLI and list again

errors.means: hooks.json is malformed, so the default account and server could not be read
errors.fix: Fix hooks.json, or pass --account and --server after fixing it

doors.when: Removing a webhook endpoint you no longer route, together with its undelivered events, from the receiver
doors.confirm: This deletes the hook and its pending events from the hooks receiver for good; delete it?

errors.means: No receiver address is known for the delete
errors.fix: Supply --server https://<receiver>, or set server in hooks.json

errors.means: The receiver turned the delete down with an HTTP error, such as 404 for an unknown hook
errors.fix: Check the hook name with hooks list and the account's token, then retry

errors.means: No GitHub CLI token exists for the account doing the delete
errors.fix: Log that account into gh, then rerun the delete

doors.when: Checking webhook routing health: per-hook session, pending count, last error, and receiver hooks nobody routes

errors.means: hooks.json has a bad entry, so no hook lines were built
errors.fix: Repair the entry the message names, then rerun hooks status

errors.means: hooks.json cannot be read because of its owner or permissions
errors.fix: Make hooks.json readable by your user and rerun hooks status

doors.when: Before recording consent, to learn which gh login has push or fork rights on the intake repo

errors.means: No signed-in gh account can see the store with push or fork rights; each listed account carries its reason.
errors.fix: Sign in to gh with an account that can push to or fork the store, then run account again.

errors.means: The gh CLI is not installed or not on PATH, so no account could be asked.
errors.fix: Install the GitHub CLI and run account again.

errors.means: --store is not an owner/repo value.
errors.fix: Pass --store as owner/repo, for example ourostack/factory.

doors.when: After the operator chooses yes or no on sharing session facts with a given store, to save that choice locally

errors.means: The private factory state folder would sit inside a Git checkout, so nothing was written.
errors.fix: Point XDG_STATE_HOME at a directory outside any Git checkout and record consent again.

errors.means: A flag failed validation (--store not owner/repo, --account not a login) or another unexpected failure; the message names which.
errors.fix: Pass --store as owner/repo and --account as a plain GitHub login.

doors.when: Started detached by Desk's session hooks to turn one session marker into a facts file in the outbox

errors.means: The marker file is gone or its fields do not form a valid marker, so nothing was derived.
errors.fix: Let the next session sweep write a fresh marker; a removed marker needs no action.

errors.means: The session log the marker points at no longer exists.
errors.fix: Check the marker's log_path; a deleted log cannot be derived again.

errors.means: Reading the marker or its session log failed partway, and the step was noted for desk_doctor.
errors.fix: Read the factory section of desk_doctor for the failed step, then rerun derive on the marker.

errors.means: The session is held back, with a reason such as no_desk_root, route_unreadable or route_unverified.
errors.fix: Read the reason field; a held marker is derived again once its route or desk root is known.

doors.when: Checking the last flush per store, held markers, pending finalize requests and retention before diagnosing delivery

errors.means: The factory state folder resolves inside a Git checkout, so status refuses to read it.
errors.fix: Set XDG_STATE_HOME to a folder outside version control and read status again.

doors.when: Pushing this machine's pending facts, labels and retractions to a consented store as one intake pull request
doors.confirm: Open or update an intake pull request on this store with this machine's pending session facts?

errors.means: This machine has no factory state or has not consented to contribute to the store.
errors.fix: Record consent with factory consent --store <owner/repo> --contribute yes first.

errors.means: Consent is recorded but names no GitHub account to deliver with.
errors.fix: Run factory account, then factory consent again with --account set to the login it names.

errors.means: Another flush holds the factory lock, so this attempt sent nothing.
errors.fix: Wait for the other flush to end and run flush again.

errors.means: The store repository could not be found from the delivering account.
errors.fix: Check the store name and that the consented account can see it.

errors.means: The consented account can neither push to nor fork the store.
errors.fix: Pick a different login with factory account and record it with factory consent.

doors.when: When the operator explicitly asks for a written explanation of one delivered job, to run the headless context writer and privacy check

errors.means: --store is not owner/repo or --job is not a 32-hex public job id.
errors.fix: Pass --store <owner/repo> and the job's 32 lowercase hex id.

errors.means: Another evaluator or context run holds the evaluator lock.
errors.fix: Wait for that run to finish and request the context again.

errors.means: This machine has no factory state folder, so there is no job to explain.
errors.fix: Record consent and let sessions be derived before requesting context.

errors.means: The command ran inside a headless factory session, which starts nothing.
errors.fix: Run context-request from an ordinary operator session.

errors.means: The headless run quota or this request's two run slots are used up.
errors.fix: Request the context again after the quota window resets.

doors.when: Once a task reaches done or cancelled, to re-derive its job's sessions and deliver them before clearing the request
doors.confirm: Deliver these finished jobs' pending session facts to their stores as intake pull requests, then start the improvement loop, which may run a headless evaluator and file kaizen issues?

errors.means: More than eight --job values were given, one repeated, or one is not 32 hex characters.
errors.fix: Pass up to eight distinct --job ids, each 32 lowercase hex characters.

errors.means: A session was still unsettled or a store flush did not deliver every file, so the finalize request was kept.
errors.fix: Read the flushes map for each store's result; the next finalize or flush retries the request.

errors.means: The finalize request was older than its time limit and was cleared without delivery.
errors.fix: Let an ordinary flush deliver the job's remaining files.

doors.when: In a store's CI, to render job pages, rollups and the index from a checked-out store into an output folder

errors.means: --out is the store itself or one of its ancestors, which the build would replace.
errors.fix: Pass an --out folder outside the store checkout.

errors.means: --store is not a real directory (a file or a symlink).
errors.fix: Pass --store as the path of the checked-out store directory.

doors.when: After the waste evaluator has written its answer files, to validate each session's labels against its brief

errors.means: --job is not a job id.
errors.fix: Pass --job with the job id the evaluate briefs name.

errors.means: A session's answer failed a check; its errors list codes such as job_mismatch, schema_outdated or too_large.
errors.fix: Rewrite that session's answer from its brief and run evaluate-accept again.

errors.means: No answer file was written for a session yet.
errors.fix: Have the evaluator write the session's answer at the brief's output path.

errors.means: A brief on disk does not match its job or file name, so its answer was not read.
errors.fix: Prepare the briefs again with factory evaluate.

doors.when: When a desk task finishes, to queue waste labeling for its sessions and write the evaluator's brief files

errors.means: --desk is not absolute, --task is missing, or --task is not <track>/<slug> or desks/<alias>/<track>/<slug>.
errors.fix: Pass an absolute --desk and --task as track/slug, or pass --pending alone.

errors.means: The --desk folder could not be resolved, so it is probably misspelled or removed.
errors.fix: Check the path with ls and pass the real absolute desk root.

errors.means: This machine has no factory state or no consenting store, so no request was recorded.
errors.fix: Record consent for a store before asking for evaluation.

errors.means: The job has no derived sessions to label in any consenting store.
errors.fix: Let the job's sessions be derived, then run evaluate again.

doors.when: Finding the report URL for a task card's job, or with --this-machine the operator's own keyed report

errors.means: --desk was given but is not an absolute path.
errors.fix: Pass --desk as the absolute desk root the task tools see.

errors.means: The --desk folder could not be resolved.
errors.fix: Check the path with ls and run job-link again with the right root.

errors.means: The desk is known not to be private, so its card gets no plain report link.
errors.fix: Add --this-machine for the private keyed link to this machine's sessions.

errors.means: The desk's visibility has not been learned yet, so a printed link might not exist.
errors.fix: Run a flush so GitHub is asked about the desk's visibility, then retry.

errors.means: This machine has no machine secret yet, so it has published nothing keyed.
errors.fix: Let a flush deliver this machine's sessions first; job-link creates no secret.

doors.when: In a store's build, to compare each open improvement card's measure before and after its countermeasure version
doors.confirm: Create or update the check comment and verdict labels on every open kaizen issue in this store?

errors.means: --repo is not owner/repo or GH_TOKEN is empty.
errors.fix: Pass --repo <owner/repo> and set GH_TOKEN to the store's token.

errors.means: GitHub returned an issue or comment shape the client does not read; that card is marked failed.
errors.fix: Rerun the check; if it repeats, file it with friction_add including the card number.

errors.means: A card's GitHub calls failed without a named code, and the other cards were still checked.
errors.fix: Read the cards list for the failed number and rerun kaizen-check.

doors.when: In a store's build, to raise or clear alarm issues when a tracked plugin's latest version worsens a quality measure
doors.confirm: Open, update, reopen or close andon issues in this store's GitHub repository?

errors.means: The store's factory.json is not valid JSON or not the andon.plugins shape.
errors.fix: Correct factory.json in the store checkout and run andon again.

errors.means: --repo is not owner/repo or GH_TOKEN is empty.
errors.fix: Pass --repo <owner/repo> and export GH_TOKEN with the store's token.

errors.means: A GitHub issues call ran past its time limit; that alarm is reported as failed.
errors.fix: Rerun andon once GitHub responds normally.

doors.when: Auditing a time window for real task work that did not become a factory job, with a reason code per mismatch

errors.means: --desk is not absolute, --store is empty, or --since and --until are not ordered exact UTC timestamps.
errors.fix: Pass an absolute --desk and UTC --since earlier than --until, such as 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z.

errors.means: Reading the desk folder raised an exception.
errors.fix: Check that the desk folder exists and can be read, then rerun reconcile.

errors.means: Reconcile hit an unexpected failure and reported nothing.
errors.fix: Run reconcile again; if it repeats, file it with friction_add.

doors.when: Started detached at session start to route findings, run the evaluator, mirror cards and measure, within a time budget
doors.confirm: Run the improvement loop now, which may start a headless evaluator run and file kaizen issues in the desk's store?

errors.means: --desk is not absolute or --person-prefix is neither empty nor desks/<alias>.
errors.fix: Pass an absolute --desk and, for a crew member, --person-prefix desks/<alias>.

errors.means: Another loop worker holds the machine's loop lock.
errors.fix: Wait for that worker to end; the next session start runs the loop again.

errors.means: DESK_FACTORY_LOOP is set to a value other than 1, true, on or yes.
errors.fix: Unset DESK_FACTORY_LOOP or set it to 1 to turn the loop on.

errors.means: No store has contribute set to yes, so the loop starts nothing.
errors.fix: Record consent for a store with factory consent if the loop should run.

errors.means: A newer Desk release is installed than the one that started this worker, so it claimed nothing.
errors.fix: Start a new session so the newest release's hooks run the loop.

doors.when: In a store's CI, to judge whether a pull request's merged tree holds only valid published facts, labels and capture records

errors.means: The head carries merge commits of its own, which are refused.
errors.fix: Rebase the pull request head onto the base so it has no merge commits.

errors.means: Merging the head into the base conflicts, so there is no tree to judge.
errors.fix: Resolve the conflict on the head branch and push again.

errors.means: Git is older than 2.38, which git merge-tree --write-tree needs.
errors.fix: Install Git 2.38 or later and run validate-pr again.

errors.means: git merge-tree failed for a reason other than a conflict, usually a missing base or head commit.
errors.fix: Fetch both the base and head commits, then rerun validate-pr.

errors.means: Git data could not be read, usually because the working directory is not the PR's checkout.
errors.fix: Run validate-pr from the pull request's checkout.

errors.means: A non-maintainer changed a file outside facts, labels, context and capture paths.
errors.fix: Limit the pull request to published fact, label or capture files.

doors.when: Excluding a deliberate test run from measurement by flagging its recorded session marker, given its session id

errors.means: The session id is not a valid session id.
errors.fix: Pass the session's full id as the first argument.

errors.means: Nothing on this machine records the session.
errors.fix: Run proof on the machine whose desk recorded that session.

errors.means: Only the derivation ledger knows the session; its marker was pruned after 30 days.
errors.fix: Mark proof sessions within 30 days, before their marker is pruned.

errors.means: More than one host records this session id.
errors.fix: Check which host's session it is; proof marks only a single-host session.

errors.means: No desk recorded the session, its desk folder is gone, or it is not the --desk given.
errors.fix: Pass --desk as the absolute root of the desk that recorded the session.

doors.when: At the start of a session, to get the one boot report: bound desk, host, prerequisites, sync, active tasks, push accounts and open PRs

errors.means: A source names a desk whose folder is missing, unreadable or malformed, or the boot itself threw; the degraded lines say which.
errors.fix: Read the degraded lines, then call desk_status or desk_doctor to see which binding or prerequisite to fix.

errors.means: No source names a desk at all, as on a first run on this machine.
errors.fix: Set up a desk with the first-run-bootstrap skill, then boot again.

errors.means: The --task name matched more than one open task card, so no task was opened.
errors.fix: Run it again with --task set to one of the listed candidates' handle or track/slug.

errors.means: The --task name matched no open task card.
errors.fix: Check the name against the open task cards, or leave --task out.

doors.confirm: Outside a headless run, the boot may commit waiting task logs and start a background push of the desk's unpushed commits to its remote; go ahead?

doors.when: Pulling the desk's remote into the bound checkout at session start, fast-forward only, and starting delivery of local commits the remote lacks
doors.confirm: This may commit waiting task logs and start a background push of the desk's unpushed commits to its remote; go ahead?

errors.means: The sync did not resolve; a Desk problem block names the reason and what to look at.
errors.fix: Follow the block's look line, for example git status in the desk, then let the next sync catch up.

errors.means: git fetch of the upstream failed or timed out, so the checkout was left as it was.
errors.fix: Check the network and the Git sign-in for the desk's remote, then run session-sync.js again.

errors.means: Files the remote also changed are modified or untracked here, so the checkout stayed behind.
errors.fix: Commit or move the files the block lists, then run the sync again.

doors.when: From a startup hook, to learn which desk Desk's MCP server would bind here, or to print the startup and boot-check lines

errors.means: No source names a desk, so root is null, code is desk-root-not-found, and the error and tried fields list every path looked at; the exit status stays 0 so a startup hook carries on.
errors.fix: Bind a desk, for example by setting $DESK or saving a binding, then run it again.

doors.confirm: With --boot-checks this may start workspace repairs and the detached Desk-problem filer, which can open a public ourostack/desk issue; go ahead?

doors.when: Run by path from session-start hooks to fast-forward the desk's state branch, repair leftover worktrees, or run a script under a supported Node

errors.means: --fast-forward skipped: the state branch has local commits its upstream lacks.
errors.fix: Let the push worker deliver those commits, then run --fast-forward again.

errors.means: --fast-forward skipped: the branch has no remote or upstream to catch up to.
errors.fix: Set an upstream for the state branch with git branch --set-upstream-to, or keep the desk local.

errors.means: --fast-forward skipped because git fetch of the branch's remote failed.
errors.fix: Check the network and Git sign-in, then run --fast-forward again.

errors.means: --revoke refused: the worktree's closeout record names a different repository, worktree, branch or owner.
errors.fix: Pass the exact repository, worktree, branch ref and owner that the closeout record holds.

doors.when: During the 02-tidy-desk migration, to check whether this session's desk needs its one-time tidy, then claim, defer or record it

errors.means: --defer was given without a one-line reason.
errors.fix: Run tidy-status --defer with a short reason after it.

errors.means: --refresh-identity was given without --root.
errors.fix: Add --root with the Desk tools' root from desk_status.

errors.means: The desk repository is not a Git repository or is mid-merge, rebase or similar, so it printed the line to say and exited 1; with --report it also holds the tidy.
errors.fix: Say the printed line and carry on; a later session start offers the tidy again.

doors.when: In the 03-desk-release-channel migration, to move an agency.toml Desk entry pinned to main over to the release channel

errors.means: Another Desk session holds the agency.toml lock and is moving the entry now, so nothing changed.
errors.fix: Leave it; the next session start checks agency.toml again.

errors.means: agency.toml changed while this ran, so the rewrite was dropped and the file kept as it was.
errors.fix: Run it again with --migrate, or let the next session start retry.

doors.when: Started detached after a desk commit, to wait out the debounce and push the desk's unpushed commits to its remote
doors.confirm: This pushes the desk's local commits to its Git remote; go ahead?

errors.means: The push worker could not publish; local commits are kept and nothing was forced.
errors.fix: Call desk_status for the blocked reason, fix that cause, then run the recovery command the error names.

errors.means: The worker ended in a state this command does not know.
errors.fix: Call desk_status for the sync state and unpushed count, then run the recovery command the error names.

errors.means: Another push worker holds this desk's lock and pushes everything, so this run ends quietly with exit 0.
errors.fix: Wait for the holder to finish, then read desk_status to confirm the push.

doors.when: When a session's Desk tools cannot run a write, to run one task_update, task_create, task_archive or desk_save through a fresh bootstrap
doors.confirm: This runs one Desk write on that root, which commits on the desk and leaves a push to its remote pending unless --publication deferred; go ahead?

errors.means: The flags did not parse, or one was given as an empty value.
errors.fix: Pass --root and --operation with real values, and the tool input as JSON on stdin or --input-file.

errors.means: The Desk server bound a different desk than --root names, so the write was not dispatched.
errors.fix: Pass the root desk_status reports, or bind the intended desk first.

errors.means: Desk's server was not admitting or ready for writes; the report carries its status.
errors.fix: Read the status in the report, fix what it names, then run the command once more.

errors.means: A step ran past the deadline, so the report says what is known and what is uncertain.
errors.fix: Carry out the report's readback steps before trying the write again.

doors.when: When a Desk tool left a commit unfinished, to check its captured change against HEAD and the index and, with --commit, commit it once

errors.means: A check failed, such as another commit to these paths or a different staged index, so nothing was committed (exit 4).
errors.fix: Read the reason and decide by hand what those paths should hold.

errors.means: Git could not say where the change stands, or a hook or the branch update was cut off (exit 5).
errors.fix: Read HEAD and git log for the commit the answer names before running it again.

doors.when: Started detached by a boot check after a Desk mechanism failed, to file it as a public ourostack/desk issue or count a known one
doors.confirm: This opens, or comments on, a public issue on ourostack/desk from a signed-in GitHub account; go ahead?

errors.means: No signed-in, unmanaged GitHub account can see ourostack/desk, so nothing was filed; the run stays silent.
errors.fix: Sign in a personal account with gh auth login; a later session start can file it.

errors.means: Today's cap on Desk problems filed from this machine is reached, so no issue was opened.
errors.fix: Wait for a later day's session start, or report it by hand with the desk-problem skill.

errors.means: The local count of this hit could not be written; a stderr line names it.
errors.fix: Run the same command again so the hit is counted.

doors.when: To browse the published factory site locally with this desk's real task names, served on 127.0.0.1 until stopped

errors.means: No desk is bound on this machine.
errors.fix: Bind a desk with desk_start, then run private-view again.

errors.means: The view folder sits inside a Git work tree, where the task names could be committed.
errors.fix: Point XDG_STATE_HOME at a folder outside every Git work tree, then run it again.

errors.means: This desk's visibility is not known yet, so its job IDs cannot be derived.
errors.fix: Run a factory flush, then run private-view again.

errors.means: The machine secret that keys this desk's job IDs does not exist yet.
errors.fix: Run a factory flush to create the secret, then start private-view once more.

doors.when: Registered as the host's session-end and stop hook: it records the session's facts in the background and, at a stop, checks the final reply is verified

errors.means: The background worker could not start or timed out, so the session's facts were not captured; it prints an unverified line and exits 0.
errors.fix: Run factory status, then flush; the next session end retries.

errors.means: The delivery check could not run at a stop, so the final reply is unverified; it exits 0.
errors.fix: Check the final reply against the delivery rules yourself before finishing.

errors.means: The reply was already corrected once and the stop hook is active again, so it lets the stop through unverified.
errors.fix: Check the final reply against the delivery rules yourself before finishing.

doors.when: Started detached by session-start hooks when a store opts in, to sweep session markers, flush facts and refresh andon issues
doors.confirm: This delivers pending session facts to each opted-in GitHub store and updates its andon issues; go ahead?

errors.means: The 120-second budget ran out before a store's flush or andon refresh, so that store waits.
errors.fix: Let the next session start flush it, or run factory flush for that store.

errors.means: Another flush held the factory state lock until the deadline, so this store sent nothing.
errors.fix: Wait for that flush to end; the next session start retries.

errors.means: The store's consent record names no account to deliver with.
errors.fix: Record an account with factory consent, then flush again.

errors.means: GitHub answered 404 for the store repository.
errors.fix: Check the store name in the consent record and the account's access to it.

doors.when: Started detached at session start, to launch the factory improvement loop worker for the bound desk under a hard stop
doors.confirm: This starts the factory loop, which may run a headless evaluator and file kaizen issues; go ahead?

errors.means: Explicit arguments were not exactly --desk <absolute path> --person-prefix <empty or desks/alias>.
errors.fix: Pass both flags in that order, or no arguments to use the bound desk.

errors.means: No bound desk was found, so nothing started.
errors.fix: Bind a desk, or pass --desk with its absolute path.

errors.means: The person whose desk this is could not be resolved without a network call.
errors.fix: Run desk_status to see the resolved person, then start it again.

errors.means: --person-prefix differs from the person resolved for that desk.
errors.fix: Pass the person prefix desk_status reports for that desk.

errors.means: DESK_FACTORY_LOOP is set to something other than 1, true, on or yes, which switches the loop off.
errors.fix: Unset DESK_FACTORY_LOOP, or set it to 1, to let the loop run.

doors.when: How hosts launch the Desk tool server under whatever node they found: it picks a compatible Node and runs index.js in it

errors.means: No installed Node satisfies Desk's engines range, so every tool answers degraded with this machine's install command.
errors.fix: Run the install command the answer names, then reconnect the Desk server.

errors.means: A compatible Node was found but could not be started.
errors.fix: Check that Node runs from a shell, or reinstall it, then reconnect.

errors.means: Something threw while picking or starting a Node, so the tools answer degraded.
errors.fix: Read the [desk-mcp] bootstrap line on stderr, fix what it names, then reconnect.

doors.when: Starting Desk's stdio tool server directly in a supported Node, with --root or an activation config, as the bootstrap does

errors.means: This Node is older than Desk's engines floor and no compatible Node could take over.
errors.fix: Install a Node at or above the floor, or start the server through bootstrap.cjs.

errors.means: The offline runtime pack could not be restored, so the server starts degraded.
errors.fix: Run desk_doctor for the pack's state, then reconnect.

errors.means: Another process held the runtime publication lock for the whole wait, so this one started degraded.
errors.fix: Wait for that process to finish restoring, then call desk_status.

errors.means: A launcher passed --degraded with a code outside Desk's pattern, so every data tool is refused.
errors.fix: Fix what the launcher reported, then start the server without --degraded.

doors.when: How hosts launch Desk's headless browser server, which opens throwaway or copied-profile browsers for browser_context and browser_command

errors.means: A tool call named something other than browser_context or browser_command.
errors.fix: Call one of those two tools, by the names the server lists.

doors.when: Before dispatching a Superpowers implementer or reviewer, to map a task's brief, report, review and progress paths inside the desk

errors.means: --desk-root, --task-path or --iteration-path is missing; the message shows an example path.
errors.fix: Pass the flag the message names, shaped like the example it gives.

errors.means: An argument is not one of the flags the mapper knows.
errors.fix: Remove that argument and keep to the mapper's flags, such as --desk-root, --task-path and --iteration-path.

errors.means: A flag was given with no value after it.
errors.fix: Put the value right after that flag.

errors.means: --plan-path points outside the desk.
errors.fix: Pass a plan file inside the desk root, or leave --plan-path out.

doors.when: In CI or before merging, to hold AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and similar instruction files to the byte budgets in .github/agents-md-budget.json

errors.means: An instruction file is bigger than its budget, so the check exits 1.
errors.fix: Turn a rule into a check or delete one, or raise the budget with --set and say why in the pull request.

errors.means: An instruction file has no budget yet, so the check exits 1.
errors.fix: Run it with --set to record today's sizes as the budgets.

doors.when: Before adding binaries to a repository, to see its Git LFS tool, filters, hooks and which tracked files are pointers

errors.means: The --repo folder is missing, not a folder, or not a Git repository, so the command exits 1.
errors.fix: Pass --repo with the path of an existing Git checkout.

errors.means: Git could not read the repository's top level, config or index, so the report stops there.
errors.fix: Run git status in that checkout to see Git's own error, then inspect again.

errors.means: The time or byte budget ran out, so the report is limited.
errors.fix: Treat files the report leaves out as not checked.

errors.means: A tracked file reads as an LFS pointer but does not parse as a valid one; the finding names its path.
errors.fix: Restore that file from its real content and add it again under LFS.

doors.when: When agent session storage, worktrees or logs grow large, to list what is safe to remove and, with --apply, delete it

errors.means: --skip named something other than logs, sessions, worktrees or state.
errors.fix: Pass --skip with only those names.

errors.means: The app database could not be read, so sessions and worktrees were left untouched and the report says so.
errors.fix: Check the app database path the line names, then run it again.

doors.when: Before publishing a pull request, to check its body carries a rendered image or a specific No visual change reason

errors.means: The body has neither a hosted inline image nor a specific No visual change reason, so it exits 1.
errors.fix: Add a rendered capture as an inline image, or No visual change: followed by a specific reason.

errors.means: The change is marked visual (--visual-change yes) but the body says No visual change, so it exits 1.
errors.fix: Capture the changed surface with safe data and drop the No visual change line.

errors.means: The arguments were wrong: no or several of --stdin, --body and --event, a missing file, or a bad --visual-change value; it exits 2.
errors.fix: Pass exactly one of --stdin, --body <file> or --event <file>, and --visual-change yes, no or unknown.

errors.means: The --event file has no pull_request.body, so it exits 2.
errors.fix: Pass the pull_request event JSON the workflow received.

errors.means: The body or event file could not be read or parsed, so it exits 2.
errors.fix: Check the file path and that an --event file is valid JSON.

doors.when: A wake runner's one stable entry for the drains CLI: it fetches the released Desk and runs drains.js with the arguments given

errors.means: GitHub could not be reached or the fetch failed, so the last published copy of Desk runs; one line goes to stderr and resolve.log.
errors.fix: Nothing is needed unless the line repeats; check network access to github.com.

errors.means: No released Desk could be resolved from the cache and there is no last good path, so it exits 1 without running anything.
errors.fix: Check the line's reason, run a Desk update or restore access to github.com, then start the runner again.

doors.when: Checking whether any Copilot server runtime on this machine started without Desk's plugin, so its sessions have no desk tools

errors.means: ps could not list this host's processes, so no runtime was checked and it exits 1.
errors.fix: Run ps -axo pid=,command= yourself to see why it fails, then run runtimes status again.

doors.when: Listing the plugin folders whose migrations Desk's session start walks, one per plugin from Agency's cache

errors.means: --engine named an engine Agency does not cache plugins for, so it exits 2.
errors.fix: Pass --engine copilot or --engine claude, or leave it out for copilot.

doors.when: Asked who must approve an Azure DevOps pull request, to map its changed files to required reviewer groups and rank approvers

errors.means: The active az account is not in the expected tenant, so no request was sent, the result is empty and it exits 3.
errors.fix: Run az login --tenant microsoft.onmicrosoft.com, then run the audit again.

errors.means: az could not issue an Azure DevOps bearer token, so the result is empty and it exits 3.
errors.fix: Check az account show and sign in again with az login.

errors.means: An Azure DevOps request failed, so it prints the HTTP error and exits 1.
errors.fix: Check the org, project, repository GUID and PR number, and the account's access to them.

doors.when: The companion's HTTP and WebSocket server itself, normally launched by start-server.sh with BRAINSTORM_DIR and friends in its environment

errors.means: BRAINSTORM_OWNER_PID was already dead at startup, so the owner watchdog is off and only the idle timeout stops the server.
errors.fix: Stop it with stop-server.sh when done, or pass a live owner PID next start.

errors.means: The server shut down because its owner process exited or it sat idle past the timeout (4 hours by default).
errors.fix: Start a fresh session with start-server.sh and reopen the printed URL.

errors.means: The saved port was taken, so the server bound a random port and, because the key came from .last-token, a new key; an open tab on the old URL no longer connects.
errors.fix: Open the new url from the server-started line.

doors.when: Once the person agrees to the visual companion, launching a server session and getting its URL and screen folder back as JSON

errors.means: An option the script doesn't know was passed; it prints a JSON error and exits 1.
errors.fix: Pass only --project-dir, --host, --url-host, --idle-timeout-minutes, --open, --foreground or --background.

errors.means: --idle-timeout-minutes was not a positive whole number.
errors.fix: Pass a whole number of minutes, 1 or more.

errors.means: The --project-dir folder could not be created or entered.
errors.fix: Pass a folder path this user can create and write.

errors.means: The server started but the environment reaped the background process.
errors.fix: Rerun with --foreground in a persistent terminal, as the error message prints.

errors.means: No server-started line reached the log within 5 seconds.
errors.fix: Read state/server.log in the session folder for the reason, then start again.

doors.when: Ending a companion session: stops the server whose instance id matches, and deletes the session folder only when it sits under /tmp

errors.means: No session folder argument was given.
errors.fix: Pass the session folder start-server.sh created, the parent of its state folder.

errors.means: The pid file names a process that is gone or lacks this session's instance id, or the instance id file is missing; nothing was signalled and it exits 0.
errors.fix: Nothing to stop; start a new session if one is still needed.

errors.means: The server was still running after SIGTERM and SIGKILL.
errors.fix: Find the process by its --brainstorm-server-id argument and end it by hand.

errors.means: The session has no pid file, so no server was running for it.
errors.fix: Check the session folder path, or treat the session as already stopped.

doors.when: Starting one task of an inline plan run: writes its brief and prints the brief path plus the BASE commit in one call

errors.means: It was not given exactly a plan file and a task number; exit 2.
errors.fix: Call it as task-start PLAN_FILE TASK_NUMBER.

errors.means: The current folder is outside a Git working tree or the repository has no commit yet; exit 2.
errors.fix: Run it from inside the working tree being executed in, after a first commit.

errors.means: task-brief found no heading Task N in the plan and exited 3, which stops task-start with no brief.
errors.fix: Check the task number against the plan's Task headings, written with the English word Task.

doors.when: Closing an inline plan task: runs its test command, keeps the full log, and appends the completion line to the ledger only on success

errors.means: The arguments were not PLAN_FILE TASK_NUMBER BASE -- TEST_COMMAND; exit 2.
errors.fix: Pass the BASE task-start printed, then -- and the test command.

errors.means: BASE is not a commit in the working tree's repository; exit 2.
errors.fix: Pass the full SHA that task-start printed for this task.

errors.means: The test command exited non-zero, so the task was not recorded and its exit status is returned.
errors.fix: Read the task's tests log in the workspace, fix the failure and run task-done again.

doors.when: While writing or editing a skill, to render the dot diagrams in its SKILL.md to SVG files next to it, or into one combined SVG with --combine

errors.means: No skill folder was given, so it prints its usage and exits 1.
errors.fix: Pass the skill's folder, optionally with --combine.

errors.means: The folder has no SKILL.md, so it exits 1.
errors.fix: Pass the skill's own folder, the one that holds SKILL.md.

errors.means: The dot program is not installed, so it prints install hints and exits 1.
errors.fix: Install graphviz (brew install graphviz or apt install graphviz), then run it again.

doors.when: Finding the top folder of the Git working tree the plan scripts act in, optionally insisting it already has a commit

errors.means: An argument other than --with-commit was passed; exit 2.
errors.fix: Call it with no arguments or with --with-commit only.

errors.means: The current folder is outside a working tree, or with --with-commit the repository has no commit; git's own line follows; exit 2.
errors.fix: Change into the working tree being executed in, or make a first commit in a new project.

doors.when: Getting, and creating if needed, one plan's scratch folder under .superpowers/sdd for briefs, reports, review packages and its ledger

errors.means: The folder given with -C does not exist; exit 2.
errors.fix: Pass -C with an existing checkout or worktree folder.

errors.means: The argument count was wrong, the plan file path does not name a file, or no workspace name can be derived from it; exit 2.
errors.fix: Pass the path of the plan's Markdown file.

errors.means: sdd-repo found no Git working tree at the current or -C folder; exit 2.
errors.fix: Run it inside the working tree being executed in, or pass -C with that folder.

doors.when: Copying one task's full text out of an implementation plan into a brief file an implementer subagent reads in one call

errors.means: The plan file path does not name a file, or the argument count was wrong; exit 2.
errors.fix: Call it as task-brief [-C DIR] PLAN_FILE TASK_NUMBER [OUTFILE].

errors.means: No heading Task N matches the requested number, so the empty brief is refused; exit 3.
errors.fix: Check the number against the plan's headings, which say Task in English; if a never-closing fence is reported above, close it and rerun.

errors.means: A code fence that never closes hides the end of the task, so the brief was refused; exit 4.
errors.fix: Close the fence at the line the message names and rerun.

doors.when: Before dispatching a reviewer, writing one file with a task's commit list, file stats and the BASE..HEAD diff with extra context

errors.means: The arguments were not PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD [OUTFILE], or the plan file is missing; exit 2.
errors.fix: Call it as review-package [-C DIR] PLAN_FILE BASE HEAD [OUTFILE].

errors.means: BASE or HEAD is not a commit in the repository; exit 2.
errors.fix: Pass the BASE recorded for the task and the task's last commit.

errors.means: HEAD does not descend from BASE, or the range holds no commits; exit 3.
errors.fix: Check out the task's branch, or pass the right BASE, so BASE..HEAD holds the task's commits.

doors.when: A test run leaves a stray file such as .git behind and the guilty test is unknown; runs npm test on each matching file in turn

errors.means: It was not given exactly a path to watch and a test file pattern; exit 1.
errors.fix: Call it as find-polluter.sh <path to check> <test pattern>.

errors.means: A test file created the watched path; the script names it and exits 1.
errors.fix: Run that test alone with npm test and fix its cleanup.

errors.means: The watched path existed before a test ran, so that test was skipped; if it existed from the start every test is skipped and it still reports all tests clean and exits 0.
errors.fix: Delete the watched path and run the search again.
